children.name: Philydrum lanuginosum Banks & Sol. ex Gaertn.
children.description: Philydrum is a genus of tufted, herbaceous, aquatic macrophyte plants, one of three genera constituting the plant family Philydraceae. Philydrum lanuginosum is the sole known species.

children.name: Helmholtzia glaberrima  Caruel
children.description: Helmholtzia glaberrima, commonly referred to as stream lily, is a rhizomatous perennial plant which is native to New South Wales and Queensland in Australia.

children.name: Helmholtzia novoguineensis  Skottsb.
children.description: An accepted species of Helmholtzia, a genus of large rhizomatous perennial herbs in the monocot family Philydraceae (Commelinales). A rhizomatous geophyte forming robust rosettes of long ensiform (sword-shaped) leaves, its native range runs from Maluku (the Moluccas) to New Guinea, growing in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philydrella drummondii L.G.Adams
children.description: An accepted species of the monocot family Philydraceae, endemic to the southwest of Western Australia. A bulbaceous perennial herb 0.15-0.25 m high with yellow flowers borne October-November, it grows on clay soils in freshwater swamps across the Swan Coastal Plain and Jarrah Forest bioregions. WA conservation status: Not threatened.

children.name: Philydrella pygmaea  Caruel
children.description: Philydrella pygmaea is a plant species in the Philydraceae family, first described by Robert Brown in 1810 as Philydrum pygmaeum, and transferred to the genus, Philydrella in 1878 by Teodoro Caruel.
